title: Zelensky addresses US Congress by video and Biden announces $800 million aid
body:
On 16 March 2022, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky addressed the United States Congress by video from Kyiv. He asked for a no-fly zone over Ukraine, which the White House had said would count as a military escalation, and for broader U.S. economic and political sanctions on Russia. He also asked that U.S. ports be closed to Russian goods and that American companies leave the Russian market.

Zelensky said that if a no-fly zone was too much, the United States knew what kind of defence systems Ukraine needed. He told lawmakers, "We need you right now. I call on you to do more," and closed with the words "Close the skies." He thanked President Joe Biden and the United States for the aid already provided. Lawmakers gave him standing ovations at the start and end of his speech.

Later the same day Biden announced an additional 800 million dollars in security assistance for Ukraine. The package included 800 anti-aircraft systems, thousands of shoulder-mounted missiles, machine guns, grenade launchers and drones. Biden said the United States would "give Ukraine the arms to fight and defend themselves". The package was in addition to the 13.6 billion dollars in military and financial support that Biden had already approved, which did not include fighter jets or a no-fly zone.
